about: The subject of the model documentation and validation report (docs/model/validation.md, #119; rewritten for H5's candidate by step 6 of docs/research/hypotheses/H5.md, #841). scripts/validation_report.py renders the report's candidate, performance, limitations and monitoring blocks from this file and from metadata/spread_distribution_634.json. Nothing here is a result: every development result is cited by its issue and its page, and no figure is typed. A figure enters the report only through a record in docs/runs/, and publishing one is Eleonora's decision (docs/decisions/publish-rule.md).
status: Drafted by the pull request that closes #841 for Eleonora's review. The use-limitation statement below is a proposal: she decides what the project claims. docs/use-limitation.md, which the phase 2 report read, is not changed.
use_limitation: A development-stage research forecast of the SOFR − IORB spread distribution in bp. It is not registered, it has no prospective day, and nothing it has scored is a verdict. It is not a stress-warning system and not a basis for VaR, limits, liquidity or capital, or desk sizing. Its quantiles are not recalibrated; its behaviour on quarter-ends, tax dates, in 2021-23 and in the upper tail is reported in the development pages and is not settled; and it has little history in the current scarce-reserve regime. It needs revalidation at each confirmation checkpoint and after a material policy or regime change.

evidence.what: The phase 2 gbm re-scored under scoring protocol v1, with the inputs built since phase 2, against as-of persistence (B1) and the second benchmark (B2)
evidence.split: pooled, by regime, by pressure-day type of the target day, and the upper tail

evidence.what: The candidate against H2's ceiling: is more model work worthwhile, and the ruling to stop model work and go to the validation report
evidence.split: pooled, by regime, by pressure-day type, and the upper tail

evidence.what: Why the models lose in 2021-23, and what the upper tail does
evidence.split: the 2021-23 regime and the upper tail

evidence.what: The splits the headline pages lacked, and the decision day 2019-09-18 reported with and without
evidence.split: by regime and by pressure-day type, each with and without the day

evidence.what: The back-fill of 2014-18 history tested against the candidate (H4 step 3)

assumptions: The outcome is the published panel's spread in bp on the target day. It is not re-derived from first-published vintages (scoring protocol v1, section 11; the question is open on #634).

The model is fitted on one-step pairs and read, by the as-of rule, at each lead. Whether a model trained on the pairing it is read at does better is the measurement of #449; it is open (see the open questions).
A forecast reads exactly what was public at its decision instant, per field (docs/decisions/information-set.md). The decision instant is 16:00 on the decision day.

The candidate was chosen among the variants scored in development by the protocol score alone, and the variant count is recorded in docs/research/progress.json. A candidate chosen on the days that scored it carries a selection effect that no development interval removes.
The regimes were drawn after the fact (metadata/evaluation_splits.json). No split is a pass requirement of the protocol.
limitations: Development data only. Scoring protocol v1 (#640) takes a verdict from prospective confirmation days alone, so nothing in this report supports, kills or registers the candidate.
Nothing is registered and the candidate is not in the live record. The confirmation design is decided on #733; no registration happens before it.

The quantiles come from an uncalibrated gradient-boosted fit at the protocol's grid of levels. Interval coverage and per-regime reliability are measured on the pages cited, and the model has no calibration layer to correct what they find (#753, #785, #786).

The regimes after 2020 carry the evidence that matters and the history there is short. The 2021-23 regime, where every phase 2 gbm lost to persistence, and the quarter-end and tax-date types are the splits to read first (#707, #805).
One decision day, 2019-09-18, moves the pooled comparison with the benchmark; the pages report it with and without that day (#798, #805).
The ceiling it was compared with (H2's cross-fitted fit) is not an upper bound, so "no headroom" means that this ceiling shows no better forecast, not that none exists (#758).
The Treasury clearing mandate will change the composition of SOFR after the panel ends; the drift is not in any development day (the clearing block below).
The scarcity state is not a model input (Eleonora's ruling on #157). The as-of scarcity-state split of protocol section 7 was not run (#758).
open_questions: Whether the declared candidate stays the one-step gbm_funding or becomes the direct-pairs twin: #449, measured on the pull request that closes it. The report follows the candidate that is in force when it is read.

Whether any development figure should be published as a record in docs/runs/ so that this report can state it. Publishing is Eleonora's (docs/decisions/publish-rule.md). Until she does, the report cites each result by its issue and states none.
The wording of the use-limitation statement above, which this pull request proposes.

monitoring.live_record: The live record (#215) logs the published model at the pinned commit (metadata/live_pin.json), not the candidate. The candidate has no logged day. A registered candidate joins the live record only by Eleonora's attested approval and a change of the live pin, which are hers alone (docs/decisions/drafts/owner-attestation.md).
monitoring.checkpoints: After registration, confirmation days accumulate under scoring protocol v1. At each checkpoint named in docs/research/hypotheses/H5.md the outcomes analysis and this monitoring section are updated with that checkpoint's verdict or "continue".
monitoring.revalidation: The revalidation triggers are proposed, not decided, in docs/use-limitation.md. They apply to the candidate as they did to the phase 2 model, and they are Eleonora's to decide.
